newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end 1996 at record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end 1996 at record high.

text.p: Australian shares closed at record levels on Tuesday in a holiday-shortened session where the few brokers on deck put a positive spin on the last day of 1996.
The All Ordinaries index closed the year 11.7 points higher at 2,424.6 after reaching a record intra-day high of 2426.5, surpassing the previous record high of 2416.8 set on Monday.
The index gained 10 percent over calendar 1996.

The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said the value of share trading on the ASX leapt 40 percent to a record A$186 billion (US$148 billion) in calendar 1996, a daily average of A$732 million. Total market capitalisation jumped 18 percent to A$391 billion over the year.

While end of year window-dressing and futures-led buying as the December Share Price Index futures contract closed out provided most of the momentum, brokers said the overall tone was one of confidence.

"The U.S. seems to be a significant factor in recent times. The fact that they went down but then bounced up has given us a bit more confidence that there won't be a correction," said analyst David Perry of Melbourne-based Austock Brokers, adding that interest in the resource leaders had boosted sentiment in the last two days.
"The resources stocks have been up a bit and there is a bit of interest creeping back into that area."
While Perry noted portfolio shuffling as the year ended was occurring, the level remained difficult to quantify.
"There is some speculative end of year activity but I'm not sure how much there is," he said.

Catching trader's eyes on the last day of 1996 was Papuan New Guinea mining investor, Orogen Minerals, which continued its recent strong rise as investors sought exposure to the PNG resource sector. Since listing on November 1, 1996, its shares have risen 43 percent to A$2.93 (US$2.33).
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
